info.description: HTTP API of CandleStack, a lab for experiments on financial time series. Market data covers crypto from Binance and US stocks from Alpaca. Times in responses are UTC epoch seconds; requests also accept ISO 8601. Errors are RFC 9457 problem details (`application/problem+json`). [Website](https://candlestack.tech) · [Source code](https://github.com/CandleStack-FEI-STU/candlestack) · [Status](https://ops.candlestack.tech)
info.title: CandleStack API

them does not.

The body is compact JSON: deploy checks look for `"version":"<version>"` and the commit.

get.description:
Redirects to the provider's sign-in page, or to `/signin?error=failed` when sign-in
with it is not available or this address made too many sign-in requests in a minute. A
provider's account that never signed in joins the CandleStack user with its email, so the
email links a user's GitHub and Google; it signs in to a new user when no user has it.

With `intent=connect` (signed in, a link of Settings) the provider's account is added to
the signed-in user's sign-in methods instead: the callback returns to `next` (default
`/settings/sign-in`), or to `/settings/sign-in?error=taken` when that account already
signs in to another CandleStack user, or `/settings/sign-in?error=failed`, also right away
when the request does not come from the app's own pages.

get.description:
Searches the instruments of both markets: every Binance spot pair that is trading and
every active tradable US stock and ETF at Alpaca (without OTC). Each item carries its last
price, 24 h change and 24 h volume in USD, refreshed every few minutes, and its last 10 daily
candles (`spark`), refreshed once a day (null without them).

Ranking: the top pair of a crypto base asset equal to the query (`btc` finds `BTCUSDT`
first), exact symbol, the other pairs of that base asset, symbol prefix, prefix of a word
in the name, substring of the symbol, substring of the name; ties go to `sort`, then to the
shorter symbol, then alphabetically. Without `q`, every instrument comes back in `sort`:
the most traded first by default.
`exchange` narrows any of these to the instruments that trade on it.
`total` counts all matches: page through them with `offset` and `limit`.

When the instrument list of one market cannot be loaded, the other market is still
searched and `unavailable` names the missing one; 503 when no market can be searched.

parameters.description: Symbol or name, case-insensitive; separators in symbols are ignored (`btc/usdt` finds `BTCUSDT`, `brkb` finds `BRK.B`). Without it, every instrument in symbol order.

get.description:
Closed candles of one instrument and timeframe: those with `start <= t < end`, or, without
`start`, the last `limit` before `end`.

Stocks have regular-session candles only (09:30-16:00 New York), aligned to the session
open. Missing candles are never filled; `meta.gaps` reports them. Limits: `max_candles`
expected candles per request (see the instrument detail) and a per-minute number of
candle and instrument requests per client address.

parameters.description: Start of the period, inclusive: UTC epoch seconds or ISO 8601 (`2024-06-03`, `2024-06-03T13:30:00Z`; without an offset it is UTC). Without it, the period starts where the last `limit` candles before `end` begin; `meta.start` tells where. Not together with `limit`.
parameters.name: start

schema.description: Start of the period, inclusive: UTC epoch seconds or ISO 8601 (`2024-06-03`, `2024-06-03T13:30:00Z`; without an offset it is UTC). Without it, the period starts where the last `limit` candles before `end` begin; `meta.start` tells where. Not together with `limit`.
schema.title: Start

parameters.description: End of the period, exclusive, in the same formats; default now.
parameters.name: end

schema.description: End of the period, exclusive, in the same formats; default now.
schema.title: End

parameters.description: Without `start`: how many of the newest candles before `end` to return, default 500 (`max_candles` when that is lower). Stocks count only candles of trading sessions (nights, weekends and holidays are skipped), crypto counts every candle. Fewer come back when the data starts later. Not together with `start` (422 `validation`). Above 5000 it is a 422 `validation`; when the server's `max_candles` (see the instrument detail) is below that, a `limit` above it is `too-many-candles`.
parameters.name: limit

schema.description: Without `start`: how many of the newest candles before `end` to return, default 500 (`max_candles` when that is lower). Not together with `start` (422 `validation`). Above 5000 it is a 422 `validation`; when the server's `max_candles` (see the instrument detail) is below that, a `limit` above it is `too-many-candles`.
schema.title: Limit

get.description: The instrument's logo from logo.dev (a stock by its ticker, a crypto pair by its base asset), or one fallback image when there is none, so an `` always gets a picture.
